# 0 · The problem

## Imagine this on a real Data Science team

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple big">BEFORE</span>

```text
notebook.ipynb
       ↓
"I changed the model"
       ↓
final_model_v7_FINAL.ipynb
       ↓
Slack / Teams
       ↓
"Which file is latest?"
```

</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue big">ASK THE TEAM</span>

<div class="question">Who changed it?</div>
<div class="question">What exactly changed?</div>
<div class="question">Can we review it?</div>
<div class="question">Can we go back?</div>
<div class="question">Can two scientists work at once?</div>

</div>

</div>


# The first MVP

<div class="center-v">

<div class="mvp">

<div class="title">MVP #0 · LOCAL PROJECT</div>

<div class="flow">
<span class="big node">data.csv</span>
<span class="big arrow">→</span>
<span class="big node">notebook.ipynb</span>
<span class="big arrow">→</span>

</div>

# 1 · Git vs GitHub

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple big">GIT</span>
<h2>Version control</h2>
<ul>
<li>Runs locally</li>
<li>Records changes</li>
<li>Creates commits</li>
<li>Lets you compare and restore work</li>
</ul>

```bash
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Initial setup"
```

</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue big">GITHUB</span>
<h2>Collaboration platform</h2>
<ul>
<li>Hosts Git repositories</li>
<li>Pull Requests</li>
<li>Code review</li>
<li>Issues and Actions</li>
</ul>

</div>

</div>

<div class="footer-bar">
<p><strong>Simple distinction:</strong> Git is the version control system. GitHub is where the team collaborates around Git.</p>
</div>



# 2 · Iteration 1 — Start tracking changes

## Run this in VS Code

```bash
git init
git status
```

Then:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Initial project setup"
```

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="check">
<h3>What just happened?</h3>
<p>Git created a repository and recorded the first checkpoint.</p>
</div>

<div class="mvp">
<div class="title">MVP #1</div>
<p><strong>We have version history.</strong></p>
</div>

</div>



# A commit = a useful checkpoint

<div class="grid-3">

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple big">BAD</span>

```bash
git commit -m "stuff"
```

</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple big">BETTER</span>

```bash
git commit -m "changes"
```

</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green big">GOOD</span>

```bash
git commit -m \
"Add baseline churn analysis"
```

</div>

</div>

<div class="footer-bar big">
<p>A good commit message answers: <strong>What changed?</strong></p>
</div>



# 3 · Read the history

## The team should be able to answer "what happened?"

```bash
git log --oneline
```

Example:

```text
a91f4d2 Add baseline churn analysis
31c72a1 Initial project setup
```

Then inspect:

```bash
git show a91f4d2
git diff
```

<div class="answer">
<strong>Try it:</strong> make a tiny change, commit it, then use <code>git log --oneline</code> to find your checkpoint.
</div>



# 4 · Iteration 2 — Put it on GitHub

## Local → remote

```bash
git branch -M main

git remote add origin \
https://github.com/YOUR-ORG/churn-project.git

git push -u origin main
```

<div class="flow">
<span class="node big">Your computer</span>
<span class="arrow big">git push →</span>
<span class="node main big">GitHub / main</span>
</div>

<div class="mvp">
<div class="title">MVP #2 · SHARED REPOSITORY</div>
<p>Local + versioned + available to the team.</p>
</div>



# Clone · Pull · Push

<div class="grid-3">

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple">FIRST TIME</span>
<h2><code>clone</code></h2>

```bash
git clone <url>
```

<p>Get the repository.</p>
</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue">GET UPDATES</span>
<h2><code>pull</code></h2>

```bash
git pull
```

<p>Bring remote changes to your local branch.</p>
</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green">SEND WORK</span>
<h2><code>push</code></h2>

```bash
git push
```

<p>Send your commits to GitHub.</p>
</div>

</div>



# 5 · Iteration 3 — Branches

## Don't experiment directly on <code>main</code>

```bash
git switch -c feature/preprocessing
```

<div class="branch-demo">

<div class="branch-line"></div>
<div class="branch-feature"></div>
<div class="branch-curve"></div>

<div class="branch-label main small">main</div>
<div class="branch-label feature small">feature/preprocessing</div>

<div class="dot" style="left:28%;top:35%"></div>
<div class="dot" style="left:45%;top:35%"></div>
<div class="dot" style="left:62%;top:35%"></div>
<div class="dot feature" style="left:40%;top:70%"></div>
<div class="dot feature" style="left:55%;top:70%"></div>
<div class="dot feature" style="left:70%;top:70%"></div>

</div>

<div class="footer-bar">
<p><strong>Branch = a safe place to make a change without moving <code>main</code>.</strong></p>
</div>



# Common branches in Data Science

<div class="grid-3">

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple">FEATURE</span>
<p><code>feature/clean-missing-values</code></p>
</div>

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple">FEATURE</span>
<p><code>feature/random-forest</code></p>
</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue">EXPERIMENT</span>
<p><code>experiment/xgboost</code></p>
</div>

</div>

<div class="check">
<p><strong>Important:</strong> a branch is not a separate repository. It is another line of development inside the same repository.</p>
</div>



# Branch → Commit → Push

## The daily mechanics

<div class="step-row">

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">1</div>
<p>Create branch</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">2</div>
<p>Make changes</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">3</div>
<p>Commit</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">4</div>
<p>Push</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">5</div>
<p>Open PR</p>
</div>

</div>

```bash
git switch -c feature/new-model

git add .
git commit -m "Add baseline model"

git push -u origin feature/new-model
```



# 🧪 Quick Check

## Which command creates a new branch and switches to it?

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card">
<p><strong>A</strong></p>

```bash
git branch feature/model
```

<p><strong>B</strong></p>

```bash
git switch -c feature/model
```

</div>

<div class="card">
<p><strong>C</strong></p>

```bash
git checkout main
```

<p><strong>D</strong></p>

```bash
git push origin main
```

</div>

</div>

<div class="spacer"></div>

<details>
<summary>Reveal answer</summary>

<p><strong class="green-text">B · <code>git switch -c feature/model</code></strong></p>
<p>It creates the branch and switches your working tree to it.</p>

</details>



# 6 · Pull Requests

## A Pull Request is where the team reviews a change

<div class="flow big">
<span class="node feature big">feature/model</span>
<span class="arrow big">→ Pull Request →</span>
<span class="node main big">main</span>
</div>

<div class="grid-3">

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple big">AUTHOR</span>
<p>Explain the change.</p>
</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue big">REVIEWER</span>
<p>Ask questions and suggest improvements.</p>
</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green big">CI</span>
<p>Run automated checks.</p>
</div>

</div>



# What happens in a PR?

<div class="step-row">

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">1</div>
<p>Open PR</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">2</div>
<p>CI checks</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">3</div>
<p>Review</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">4</div>
<p>Changes</p>
</div>

<div class="step big">
<div class="num">5</div>
<p>Merge</p>
</div>

</div>

<div class="footer-bar">
<p>The important part is not the button you click. It's the <strong>shared review before the change reaches main</strong>.</p>
</div>



# 🧪 Practice — Read the workflow

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card purple">
<span class="label label-purple big">SCENARIO</span>
<p>A scientist is improving preprocessing.</p>

```text
main
  │
  └── feature/model
        │
       C1
        │
       C2
        │
       C3
        └────→ Pull Request
```

</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue big">YOUR TURN</span>

<div class="question">Which branch is being worked on?</div>
<div class="question">Where is the Pull Request coming from?</div>
<div class="question">What happens after review and CI pass?</div>

<details>
<summary>Reveal answers</summary>
<p>Feature branch → Pull Request → merge into <code>main</code>.</p>
</details>

</div>

</div>



# 7 · Merge conflicts

## Git can detect a conflict. It cannot decide the meaning.

Two scientists change the same line:

```python
threshold = 0.50
```

vs.

```python
threshold = 0.65
```

Git may show:

```text
<<<<<<< HEAD
threshold = 0.50
=======
threshold = 0.65
>>>>>>> feature/model
```

<div class="answer">
<strong>Human decision:</strong> choose the correct value, edit the file, then stage and commit the resolution.
</div>



# Conflict resolution

```bash
git status
```

Fix the file.

Then:

```bash
git add .
git commit -m "Resolve threshold conflict"
```

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple">GIT DOES</span>
<p>Detect the conflicting lines.</p>
</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green">HUMANS DO</span>
<p>Decide what the code should mean.</p>
</div>

</div>



# 8 · `.gitignore`

## Don't commit everything

```text
data/
.env
__pycache__/
.ipynb_checkpoints/
*.pyc
credentials.json
```

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple">KEEP OUT</span>
<p>Local environments, secrets, generated files and large local data.</p>
</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green">REMEMBER</span>
<p>GitHub is collaboration infrastructure — not a place to casually publish sensitive data.</p>
</div>

</div>

# 12 · GitHub Actions

## What if every Pull Request tested itself?

<div class="flow">
<span class="node feature big">Pull Request</span>
<span class="arrow big">→</span>
<span class="node blue big">GitHub Actions</span>
<span class="arrow big">→</span>
<span class="node green big">Tests</span>
<span class="arrow big">→</span>
<span class="node main big">Review / Merge</span>
</div>

<div class="grid-3">

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple">INSTALL</span>
<p>Set up the environment.</p>
</div>

<div class="card blue">
<span class="label label-blue">TEST</span>
<p>Run automated checks.</p>
</div>

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green">REPORT</span>
<p>Show pass / fail on the PR.</p>
</div>

</div>



# A tiny CI workflow

Create:

```text
.github/workflows/tests.yml
```

```yaml
name: Tests

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"

      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: pytest
```



# Why CI matters in Data Science

A small code change can affect:

```text
preprocessing
      ↓
features
      ↓
training
      ↓
metrics
      ↓
reports / pipelines
```

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card green">
<span class="label label-green">PASS</span>
<p><strong>Keep reviewing.</strong></p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<span class="label label-purple">FAIL</span>
<p><strong>Investigate before merge.</strong></p>
</div>

</div>

<div class="footer-bar">
<p>CI gives the team an early signal that a change may have broken something.</p>
</div>



# 🧪 Quick Check — CI

## A Pull Request is open and CI fails. What should happen?

<div class="grid-2">

<div class="card">
<p><strong>A</strong> Merge anyway because the code looks correct.</p>
</div>

<div class="card">
<p><strong>B</strong> Investigate the failing check, fix the branch, and run CI again.</p>
</div>

</div>

<div class="spacer"></div>

<details>
<summary>Reveal answer</summary>

<p><strong class="green-text">B.</strong> The failing check is a signal to investigate before merging.</p>

</details>
